resources.string: Strohhalm keeps offline mirror copies of your git repositories. Three things are needed before it can start.

Mirrors are stored as real git repositories in a folder you choose, so they survive uninstalling the app and can be copied to a computer. Android only allows that with all-files access, which has to be granted by hand in system settings.
Pick or create a folder for the mirrors. Android does not allow choosing the top level of internal storage, so create a folder such as "Strohhalm".
Strohhalm stays quiet while backups succeed and only notifies you when one cannot run.
Strohhalm wrote a small file to the folder you chose, recording where it believes it wrote it. Find this file on your device or computer and confirm it is really at this path.
The folder could not be written to: %1$s
Add this line to the server\'s authorized_keys, or as a read-only deploy key, so Strohhalm may read the repositories.
A new key is generated and the current one stops working immediately. Every server has to be updated with the new public key before backups resume.
